entries.subject: LAM 2021 216_Kleopatra_mpcd.obj
entries.finding: LAM 2021 `216_Kleopatra_mpcd.obj` — Released detailed shape with both lobes and concave neck — Included. Original 1,586 vertices and 3,168 faces in km. The numerical volume is 865,179.55 km³, matching the MPCD paper's nominal 865,000 km³. The release has 3,168 faces whereas the paper describes 3,136; that difference is recorded rather than editing the source.

entries.subject: LAM reduced/deconvolved SPHERE images and CDS J/A+A/653/A57
entries.finding: Rebuilt 2026-09-18 by the survey setup from 30 camera-1 frames of the 2017 apparition on the ADAM mesh, and shipped on zimpol-published-comparison, the survey’s Figure B.37; the registration stage’s verdict is reported in the README. The rest of this finding describes the earlier five-frame lens: Reopened and adopted. Five deconvolved frames from the 2017 apparition are now the SPHERE photograph lens. The camera is computed, not fitted: pole, period and phase epoch come from the release’s own parameter record, observing geometry from JPL Horizons for Paranal, and plate scale, exposure time and filter from each frame’s own header. The rotation convention is Ďurech, Sidorin and Kaasalainen (2010) equation 1. Every camera field in the recipe is recomputed from the pinned parameter record, the pinned Horizons responses and each frame's own header, and compared against the recipe by a committed test, so the derivation runs rather than being asserted. An earlier revision of this lens shipped the body mirrored in longitude: atan2(y, x) in the inversion frame is an east longitude and was written into the camera's west longitude, and the north azimuth was the pole position angle turned by half a circle. The two errors cancelled in the silhouette, so the limb, disc-size and phase-angle checks all passed on the mirrored body. The handedness is now asserted directly against the transform. The paper’s caution that inferred albedo features near the limb may originate in deconvolution artefacts still stands, which is why the lens states photographed illumination and matched relative brightness rather than albedo. Removed on 2026-09-16: a lens ships only when every registration measurement that reaches a verdict places it within three degrees, and this one measured outline systematic 3.63° against relief 0.00°.

entries.subject: LAM 216_Kleopatra_param.txt
entries.finding: Resolved. The record is the standard light-curve inversion parameter layout: pole latitude, pole longitude and sidereal period on the first line, then the phase epoch and the phase at that epoch. Its column order was established against published poles rather than assumed, because the survey’s files are not consistent: most are latitude first, but at least Pallas, Hygiea, Psyche and Elektra are longitude first, and Elektra’s second value of -92.27 is not a latitude at all. Kleopatra reads latitude first. The convention was then checked against the producer’s own numbers: DAMIT distributes model 101 both as an inversion record and as IAU elements, and converting the first reproduces the second’s pole to under half a degree and its rate to 1e-4 degrees per day. The pole differs slightly from the paper’s printed values because the paper prints separate ADAM and MPCD solutions; this record describes the ADAM frame.

entries.subject: Which reconstruction the rotation parameters describe
entries.finding: The release ships two meshes for this body and one parameter record, and the record describes the ADAM reconstruction rather than the MPCD one that Marchis et al. re-optimised. Measured over seven frames and two apparitions, projecting through the ADAM mesh reproduces the observed limb position angle to 3.3 degrees; the identical parameters through MPCD give 6.8 degrees, and substituting the paper’s printed MPCD pole does not recover it. The photographic lens therefore rides the ADAM mesh while the shape view keeps MPCD, which is the shape-per-dataset pairing the celestial skill requires. Lutetia is a warning for anyone extending this: its MPCD mesh is turned 180 degrees from its ADAM mesh, so one parameter record cannot serve both. Removed on 2026-09-16: a lens ships only when every registration measurement that reaches a verdict places it within three degrees, and this one measured outline systematic 3.63° against relief 0.00°. Reinstated 2026-09-18: the rebuilt lens rides the ADAM mesh, as this finding requires, and ships on the survey’s comparison figure.

entries.subject: 2018 apparition frames and the level-matching budget
entries.finding: The 2018 apparition views the opposite hemisphere and would roughly double the photographed surface, but its frames cannot be combined with the 2017 set here. A preparation run on 2026-09-15 with all seven frames put the 2017 frames within 0.78 to 1.07 of each other and the two 2018 frames at 0.059 and 0.085, about seventeen times fainter, past this route's budget of sixteen; several cross-apparition pairs also shared no accepted samples, so that ratio is poorly constrained rather than demonstrated. Those two frames are not pinned. They were briefly retained as registration evidence, but no committed check read them, and an input that backs no reproducible claim is worse than a recorded measurement. The acquisition plan and this entry state where they are and what they showed, and the pinned Horizons tables still cover both apparitions.
entries.revisitWhen: The frames are placed on a common photometric scale, by the producers or by a documented per-frame normalisation, or enough overlapping coverage is found to constrain the ratio directly. Raising the matching budget alone would not qualify them, and re-pinning them without a committed check that reads them would not either.

entries.subject: Vernazza et al. (2021) Figure B.37 as the registration of the SPHERE photograph lens
entries.finding: Measured with tools/objects/sphere-survey/setup.mts against Vernazza et al. (2021) Figure B.37, the survey’s comparison of these frames with its models. Outline overlap with the paper’s ADAM panels 0.873 to 0.909 at our phase, against 0.930 to 0.948 for our own outline drawn at the paper’s pixel scale; over a full turn in 10° steps it peaks at our phase in 4 of 6 columns, one step from it in 2. With the paper’s photographs 0.855 to 0.925. Turned in the image, our outline best overlaps the paper’s photographs at -3.5 to 0.0° and its model panels at -3.5 to -1.5°. The spin axis we project lies at 128.8 to 131.2° on the sky against 125.1 to 128.4° for the figure’s arrows. Native outline residual 2.205 px mean over 30 frames at our phase; the sweep’s lowest is 2.174 px at -2°. The figure’s column labels were read from its pixels, and each names a frame’s exposure start to the second. The release rotation record reads latitude-first, 2.01° from the published pole.
